title: Peace Accords anniversary march opposing reelection and the state of exception
location: San Salvador; EFE identifies marchers at Plaza Gerardo Barrios in a photo caption; a second same-day report places groups near Parque Cuscatlán, with their relationship unresolved.
participants_original: EFE reports hundreds of Salvadorans (cientos de salvadoreños).
threshold_50_evidence: EFE reports hundreds of participants from civil-society, feminist and community groups at the January 15 march. This supports at least 50 people; no exact range or upper bound is provided.

start_date.summary: EFE reports the physical march on January 15, 2023; the article date and text identify that Sunday.

end_date.summary: The article does not establish when the physical gathering or march ended; null does not mean one day or month-end.

location.summary: EFE gives San Salvador and identifies marchers at Plaza Gerardo Barrios in a photo caption; no full route or endpoint is reported.

scope.summary: The report describes one public march in San Salvador by civil-society, feminist and community participants; no broader national coordination is established.

organizer.summary: Participating civil-society, feminist and community groups are described, but no specific lead organizer is identified.

demands.summary: The march opposed presidential reelection, the state of exception and arbitrary captures; the report frames demands around democracy and rights in El Salvador.

participants.summary: EFE reports hundreds of participants; it does not give precise bounds.

protester_violence.summary: The report does not establish protester violence or an explicit absence.

state_response.summary: No action by the state in response to this march is reported. Earlier arrests appear as grievances and are not coded as protest response.

notes: A public march with an own-state policy demand and a reported crowd of hundreds is supported by the direct EFE report. Attendance is not converted into fabricated numeric bounds; end and state response remain unknown. LPG S028 reports a same-day Peace Accords march around Parque Cuscatlán, but it is not included in this candidate source list because whether that report describes the same route or a separate gathering is unresolved. S029 proved to concern January 15, 2022, and is a wrong-year lead.
open_questions: Confirm whether LPG S028 covers the same physical march/route as EFE S023 or a separate gathering; do not transfer EFE attendance to another site.
Find the physical end of the march and any documented state response.
Official baseline and independent review remain pending.

title: Marcha Negra demanding pension reform and labor rights
location: San Salvador, Plaza Salvador del Mundo; the report gives Casa Presidencial as the march destination but does not establish arrival.
participants_original: ElSalvador.com reports around 1,200 people at Plaza Salvador del Mundo.
threshold_50_evidence: The report places around 1,200 attendees at Plaza Salvador del Mundo, directly supporting a simultaneous crowd of at least 50 at that site. The article does not give numerical bounds.

start_date.summary: The bylined article is dated January 27 and reports a march underway; its text says a proposal was presented that day, tying the described action to January 27. The date is inferred from same-day reporting.

end_date.summary: No time or date for the end of the physical assembly is reported. The stated destination does not establish arrival, dispersal or end.

location.summary: The article reports around 1,200 attendees at Plaza Salvador del Mundo and separately names Casa Presidencial as the march destination; arrival and full route are unverified.

scope.summary: The article describes a march in San Salvador; it does not report coordinated activity elsewhere.

organizer.summary: Social, union and labor organizations marched; a Mesa por Una Pensión Digna representative is quoted, but no single lead organizer is named.

demands.summary: Marchers called for changes to the pension law and a dignified retirement, as well as job stability and freedom of association.

participants.summary: ElSalvador.com reports around 1,200 at Plaza Salvador del Mundo; exact numeric bounds are absent.

protester_violence.summary: The report does not establish protester violence or explicitly state that none occurred.

state_response.summary: The report mentions a proposal presented that day but does not establish official receipt, negotiation, or another response.

notes: A direct bylined report supports a January 27 physical march at Plaza Salvador del Mundo, around 1,200 attendees, and demands for pension reform and labor rights. The article gives Casa Presidencial as a destination but does not confirm arrival or physical end. The same-day proposal mention is not coded as state accommodation. Figures about cotizers and dismissed employees are not turnout. No formal organizer is identified.
open_questions: Verify the physical end and whether marchers reached Casa Presidencial.
No formal state response is established by this source.
Official baseline and independent coordinator review remain pending.
